text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.25% today after oil prices dropped sharply following diplomatic signals from Iran's leadership about conditions to end the regional conflict. The stock had spiked to $151.37 yesterday when Middle East tensions were at their peak and oil was trading near $116 a barrel; today's decline mirrors the broader market reaction to reduced geopolitical risk, with crude falling back below $108.

The past week shows the direct link between regional stability and energy stocks—the company gained 5% over two weeks as tensions escalated and oil surged, but reversed course as soon as peace talks appeared more likely. This reflects how oil majors benefit from scarcity-driven price spikes, but lose those gains when the underlying supply threat recedes.
